# Consensus Algorithms: Raft vs Paxos vs PBFT

## 1. Problem Framing

### The Consensus Problem
Consensus is the fundamental challenge in distributed systems: **how do N nodes agree on a single value despite failures?**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Consensus Requirements                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Agreement    │ All non-faulty nodes decide on the same value  │
│  Validity    │ The decided value was proposed by some node     │
│  Termination  │ All non-faulty nodes eventually decide         │
│  Integrity   │ No node decides twice; values aren't corrupted  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Why It's Hard: FLP Impossibility
**Fischer, Lynch, Paterson (1985)** proved that no deterministic consensus algorithm can guarantee termination if even *one* node can fail silently. This forces practical systems to make trade-offs.

### Failure Models
| Model | Description | Real-world Example |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Crash Fault Tolerant (CFT)** | Nodes stop responding but don't lie | Hardware failures, network timeouts |
| **Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT)** | Nodes can act arbitrarily (lie, delay, equivocate) | Malicious actors, software bugs |
